subject: Migration: deployment mode selection (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@quanta-systems.com>
Cc: Priya Mehta <priya.mehta@quanta-systems.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Quick sync recap — deployment mode needs

Hi Liam / Priya,

Thanks again for the call today — good to learn more about Quanta's ingestion pipeline and where the latency and compliance pain points are. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're aligned: 

Summary of what you shared
- Current setup: production traffic is routed through another LLM API provider; you also have an internal GPU cluster used for experimental models.
- Primary pain points: inconsistent tail latency, token cost, and no simple way to enforce data residency for EU customers.
- Compliance: need SOC2 evidence and a path to PII/PHI isolation for certain customers.
- Target traffic: ~150 QPS average, spikes to ~700 QPS for some customers, typical generation length 60-120 tokens.

Deployment options we discussed
1) Hosted API (Redwood hosted) — fastest pilot, minimal infra work, immediate throughput but shared tenancy for compute. Good for PoC and low-risk customers.
2) Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) — predictable throughput, per-tenant resource isolation, SLA-backed latency guarantees. Typical path to production for customers at your scale.
3) Private (VPC / on-prem) — strict network controls and full control of data plane. Best for regulated workloads or customers that need on-prem.

Signals we heard that matter for selection
- You care about data residency + SOC2 for customer-facing compliance.
- You expect steady production scale within 2–3 months and want predictable unit economics.
- You'd like a migration path from your current API provider with as little client-side change as possible.

Proposed next steps
1) I can set up a 60-day hosted pilot (shared tenancy) so you can validate accuracy and latency with live traffic.
2) Parallel: we schedule a tech deep-dive with our infra lead (Dev) to map VPC/network requirements and an SRE session to size dedicated pool options.
3) We'll provide a draft Dedicated capacity recommendation and estimated monthly cost for your expected QPS.

Attachments: SOC2-evidence-checklist.pdf (what we can provide), redwood-deployment-matrix.xlsx (quick mapping of latency/cost tradeoffs).

Would you be open to a 45-minute tech deep dive on Tue 20 Apr or Wed 21 Apr?

Best,
Marissa

Hi Liam / team — quick pricing and infra notes from our side.

Dedicated sizing & cost (ballpark)
- 150 QPS steady; 700 QPS peaks; 60–120 token avg generation.
- Recommendation: start with a 4-slot dedicated pool (Nvidia H100-equivalent VMs, driver-managed) with autoscale headroom to 8 slots for peak. That maps to ~200–400M tokens/day depending on request mix.
- Ballpark committed monthly cost: $45k–$70k (depending on quantization/profile and connective options). This includes SLA and 24/7 support. Exact numbers after we run a cost-model with your token distribution.

Hosted pilot path
- We can spin up an isolated pilot project under hosted API in 48–72 hours. Works well for validation and accuracy checks. No infra changes client-side beyond API key and minor rate-limit tuning.

Private / on-prem considerations (Dev to add detail)
- Private VPC: straightforward; we provide a private control plane and lift-and-shift data plane to your cloud VPC. Requires network peering, NAT/firewall rules. SOC2 artifacts supported.
- On-prem: doable but requires a deployment window, offline package, and a small dedicated ops team on-site for installs/patches; timeline typically 6–10 weeks from PO.

Migration support
- We provide SDK adapters, sample traffic-splitting configs (Envoy/NGINX), and a canary rollback playbook. We'll staff an integration engineer for the migration window.

Next steps
1) Marissa: confirm pilot dates (end of May).
2) Quanta: share token distribution sample (anonymized logs) so we can run precise cost model.
3) Dev: schedule a 45-min VPC/on-prem technical deep dive (Tue 20 Apr 4pm PT suggested).

Happy to jump on a call to walk through numbers.
—Dylan
